findings.title: fc7eca35 claims resolve_function's search order was one of three CODE fixes; the commit never touches the loop order
locations: src/TestHarness.jl:304 (current `for mod in Iterators.flatten(((pkg,), modules, externals))`)
findings.before: Commit fc7eca35's message: "The state verifier found four findings still present after the pass. Three were code the earlier edit never reached — resolve_function's search order, signature_fidelity counting an extension-homed binding it skips, suspect_hats filtering seeds for one substrate out of six". At base and still at fc7eca35, the loop read `for mod in Iterators.flatten(((pkg,), externals, modules))` (Base searched before the package's own submodules) and the docstring said "externals — the external modules whose generics the package extends (searched last)".
findings.after: fc7eca35's only edit to this function is the docstring, changed to "searched after `pkg` and before `modules`" — a wording change that just restates the SAME unchanged loop order (`(pkg,), externals, modules`); `signature_fidelity` and `suspect_hats` in the same commit DO get real code changes (the `examined[] += 1` counter is moved past the extension check; `sees_seed` is added). The actual loop order does not change to `(pkg,), modules, externals` until a separate, later commit (192a336, itself part of a different round auditing this one), whose message frames it as a fresh finding ("the code put Base ahead of every package module... the order now matches it") rather than as finishing fc7eca35's claimed fix.
findings.why_it_matters: The commit message asserts three CODE-level fixes landed in this pass; only two did. A reader trusting the commit log (or `pass grade`'s per-id 'honored' disposition, which this very commit's diff writes for the finding) would believe resolve_function's Base-shadowing bug was closed at this point in the round, when the loop's actual resolution order — which determines whether a package's own `Config.read`/`Git.run`/`Scan.report` or Base's same-named export wins — was unchanged and stayed wrong for several more commits.
findings.description: This is the shape the claim-versus-edit lane exists to catch: the commit's own prose describes an edit ('code the earlier edit never reached', now presumably reached) that is not in its diff. The docstring edit is real and small, but it documents the pre-existing (still-buggy, per the later commit's own words) order rather than fixing it, so the claim overstates what this specific commit does.
findings.evidence: git show fc7eca35:src/TestHarness.jl line 303-304: `for mod in Iterators.flatten(((pkg,), externals, modules))` (identical to base 209cb21 and to 175fe95f). git show 192a3363:src/TestHarness.jl: `-    for mod in Iterators.flatten(((pkg,), externals, modules))` / `+    for mod in Iterators.flatten(((pkg,), modules, externals))`, with commit message "resolve_function promised that a package function wins its own name and the code put Base ahead of every package module; the promise was the correct one and the order now matches it."

findings.title: fc7eca35 says 'instrument' was cross-linked in eleven modules; the diff shows eight
locations: commit fc7eca35631fe20d77098cf810edd91b1290e48e — src/CLI/Audit.jl, Gate.jl, Passes.jl, RoundFiles.jl, Rounds.jl, Sync.jl, TestHarness.jl, Witnesses.jl
findings.before: Commit message: "`instrument` is cross-linked to its binding at its first docstring mention in the eleven modules that still used it bare."
findings.after: The diff adds `[`GBGCodingTools`](@ref) binds the term` (or the equivalent "one of the four review procedures … binds" phrasing) in exactly eight files: Audit.jl, Gate.jl, Passes.jl, RoundFiles.jl, Rounds.jl, Sync.jl, TestHarness.jl and Witnesses.jl. No other file in this commit's diff adds an `instrument` cross-reference.
findings.why_it_matters: Minor, but it is exactly the kind of count a later reader (or a subsequent audit pass) might cite as evidence the sweep was complete; the number in the log does not match the diff that supposedly produced it. Low stakes since the eight edits shown are all real and none is missing a link the claim would otherwise call out.
findings.description: A numeric overclaim in the commit message (11 vs 8 files touched for this specific cross-link). Could be an honest miscount rather than scope creep, and it does not correspond to any missing or extra edit found elsewhere in the round's later passes (which would have caught a truly bare 'instrument' mention).
findings.evidence: grep -c of '[`GBGCodingTools`](@ref)' / 'binds the term' / 'review procedures' across the commit's full diff returns exactly 8 matches, one per file listed above.
